items.title: Two Kinds of Knowing, and Why Dependent Origination Was Never "Made" by Anyone — Not Even the Buddha

items.zh: 應以幾智知緣起耶？答：二。謂以法住智及真實智。云何以法住智？謂如佛施設開示，無倒而知。云何以真實智？謂如學見跡，觀甚深義。問：
items.en: By how many kinds of wisdom is dependent origination known? By two: the wisdom that abides in the teaching, and genuine wisdom. What is the wisdom that abides in the teaching? Knowing, without any distortion, dependent origination exactly as the Buddha has laid it out and revealed it. What is genuine wisdom? Knowing its profound meaning directly, the way one who has already entered the noble path, having glimpsed the footprints of the path itself, actually observes it.

items.zh: 如世尊言：是諸緣起非我所作，亦非餘作。所以者何？若佛出世，若不出世，安住法性、法住、法界。云何法性？云何法住？云何法界？答：是諸緣起無始時來理成就性，是名法性。如成就性，以無顛倒文句安立，是名法住。由此法住，以彼法性為因，是故說彼名為法界。
items.en: As the Blessed One said: this dependent origination is not something I made, nor is it something anyone else made. Why is this so? Whether a buddha arises in the world or not, it abides as the nature of things, as the very standing of things, as the very realm of things. What is the nature of things? What is the standing of things? What is the realm of things? Answer: That these links of dependent origination have, since beginningless time, been a principle already fully accomplished in its own right — this is called the nature of things. That this same accomplished nature is set forth, without any distortion, in well-formed teaching — this is called the standing of things. And that this standing of things takes that very nature as its own cause — this is why it is called the realm of things.

items.zh: 問：如經言：生若無者，無處無位生可是有。若一切種生非有者，生緣老死應不可得，何故此中說彼自性緣自性耶？答：依自種子果生說故。謂識乃至受支是生種子故，義說為生。由此有故，後時即此果支名有緣生。如是餘支，如經所說，隨其所應盡當知。問：已說一切支非更互為緣，何故建立名色與識互為緣耶？答：識於現法中，用名色為緣故；名色復於後法中，用識為緣故。所以者何？以於母腹中有相續時，說互為緣故。由識為緣，於母腹中諸精血色，名所攝受，和合共成羯羅藍性。即此名色為緣，復令彼識於此得住。問：何故菩薩觀黑品時，唯至識支，其意轉還，非至餘支耶？答：由此二支更互為緣故，如識緣名色，如是名色亦緣識，是故觀心至識轉還。於餘支中，無有如是轉還道理。於此一處，顯示更互為緣道理，故名轉還。於還滅品中，名色非是後有識還滅因，由此因緣，復過觀察。問：何因緣故，說緣起支非自作、非他作、非俱作，亦非無因生耶？答：生者非有故，緣無作用故，緣力所生故。問：
items.en: Question: As the sūtra says, 'If there were no birth, there would be no place or position in which birth could exist. If birth did not exist in any way at all, old age and death conditioned by birth could not be found.' Why does it say here that a thing's own nature is the condition of its own nature? Answer: It is said with reference to the result arising from its own seeds. That is, the links from consciousness through feeling are the seeds of birth, so in meaning they are called birth. Because these exist, later this very result-link is said to be birth conditioned by existence. The remaining links, as the sūtra says, should all be understood as appropriate. Question: It has been said that no links are mutually conditioning. Why, then, are name-and-form and consciousness established as conditions of each other? Answer: Because consciousness, in the present life, uses name-and-form as its condition; and name-and-form, in a later life, uses consciousness as its condition. Why? Because they are said to condition each other when the continuity takes place in the mother's womb. With consciousness as condition, the semen and blood in the mother's womb are taken up by name and together form the kalala. With this name-and-form as condition, consciousness in turn is able to remain there. Question: Why does the bodhisattva, when contemplating the dark side, reach only the link of consciousness and then turn back, and not go on to other links? Answer: Because these two links condition each other: as consciousness conditions name-and-form, so name-and-form also conditions consciousness. So the contemplating mind reaches consciousness and turns back. Among the other links there is no such principle of turning back. Since the principle of mutual conditioning is shown in this one place, it is called turning back. In the side of cessation, name-and-form is not the cause of the cessation of consciousness in a later existence; for this reason he examines further. Question: For what reason is it said that the links of dependent arising are not made by oneself, not made by another, not made by both, and do not arise without a cause? Answer: Because there is no one who produces them, because conditions have no activity of their own, and because they arise through the power of conditions. Question:

items.title: Two Classical Images: A Sprout Tended into a Tree of Suffering, and a Lamp That Never Stops Burning

items.zh: 於緣起中，何等是苦芽，誰守養苦芽？何等為苦樹？答：無明、行緣所引識乃至受，是苦芽。受緣所引愛乃至有，是守養苦芽。生與老死，當知是苦樹。問：
items.en: Within dependent origination, what is the sprout of suffering? Who tends and waters this sprout? What is the tree of suffering? Answer: Consciousness through feeling, drawn forth by ignorance and formations as their condition, is the sprout of suffering. Craving through becoming, drawn forth by feeling as their condition, is what tends and waters the sprout of suffering. Birth and old-age-and-death, it should be understood, are the tree of suffering.

items.zh: 幾緣起支當知如炷？答：識乃至受。問：幾支如膏？答：無明、行、愛、取、有。問：幾支如焰？答：生、老死應知。問：
items.en: Which links of dependent origination should be understood as a lamp's wick? Consciousness through feeling. Which as its oil? Ignorance, formations, craving, grasping, and becoming. Which as its flame? Birth and old-age-and-death, it should be understood.

items.zh: 何因緣故，於緣起黑品教中說名增益？答：一切有支純大苦聚為後果故。又諸有支，前前為緣，後後所隨故。問：何因緣故，於白品教中說名損減？答：由一切支，前前永斷，後後減故。又是純大苦聚損減因故。問：幾緣起支名有因法？答：謂前七。問：幾緣起支名有因苦？答：餘五。問：幾支滅是漏盡所顯？答：三。問：幾支滅是緣盡所顯？答：即此三是餘支緣故。問：幾支滅是受盡所顯？答：一。謂由煩惱已斷故，所依滅時，此一切受皆永息滅故。問：
items.en: For what reason is the forward, darkened teaching of dependent origination called "accumulation"? Answer: Because every link results, in the end, in nothing but a great mass of pure suffering; and because each earlier link serves as condition for the one that follows. For what reason is the reverse, bright teaching called "diminishment"? Answer: Because as each earlier link is permanently severed, each following link ceases in turn.

items.title: Seventy-Seven Kinds of Knowledge, Then Forty-Four — Two Classical Countings from the Āgamas

items.zh: 何因緣故，依止緣起建立七十七智耶？答：為顯有因雜染智故，又復為顯於自相續自已所作雜染智故，又復為顯前際諸支無始時故，又復為顯後際諸支容有雜染還滅義故，又復為顯支所不攝諸有漏慧遍知義故。於一一支皆作七智，當知總有七十七智。問：
items.en: For what reason are seventy-seven kinds of knowledge established resting on dependent origination? Answer: To reveal the knowledge that defilement is genuinely caused; to reveal the knowledge that this defilement is one's own continuing stream's own doing; to reveal that the links of the past extend beginninglessly; to reveal that the links of the future may still admit of either defilement or purification; and to reveal the comprehensive knowledge of contaminated wisdom not itself included among the twelve links. Applying all seven of these to each single link, there are, in total, seventy-seven kinds of knowledge.

items.zh: 何因緣故，於緣起中建立四十四智耶？答：為顯於一一支，依四聖諦觀察道理，是故總有四十四智。
items.en: For what reason are forty-four kinds of knowledge established within dependent origination? Answer: To reveal, for each single link, the way of observing it through the four noble truths — and so, in total, there are forty-four kinds of knowledge.

items.zh: 復次，若生欲界，依欲界身，引發上地若眼若耳，由此見聞下地、自地所有色聲。又依此身，起三界意及不繫意而現在前。若生色無色界，除其下地，一切現前如在欲界。
items.en: Further, someone born in the desire realm, relying on a desire-realm body, can produce the eye or ear of a higher stage, and by it see and hear the forms and sounds of lower stages and of their own stage. Further, relying on this body, they can bring before them mind of the three realms and mind not bound to any realm. For someone born in the form or formless realm, everything except what belongs to lower stages can be brought before them, as in the desire realm.

items.title: Fascicle 10 Complete — and With It, the Entire Three-Grounds Section Spanning Since Fascicle 4

items.zh: 復次，此三種雜染，謂煩惱雜染、業雜染、生雜染，為欲斷故，修六種現觀應知。何等為六？謂思現觀、信現觀、戒現觀、現觀智諦現觀、現觀邊智諦現觀、究竟現觀。
items.en: Further, in order to sever these three defilements — afflictive defilement, karmic defilement, and rebirth defilement — six kinds of direct realisation should be understood as what must be cultivated. What are the six? Direct realisation through reflection, direct realisation through faith, direct realisation through moral discipline, direct realisation of the truths through wisdom, direct realisation of the truths through the wisdom bordering on that realisation, and final, complete direct realisation.

blocks.text: The last reading of fascicle 10 closes the account of dependent origination with two classical images, a tree of suffering and a lamp, and two counts of knowledge from the Āgamas. With it, the three grounds of thought, which began on Day 23, are complete. The commentary ends with a look back over the first ten fascicles.

Dependent origination is known by two wisdoms: **the wisdom that abides in the Dharma** (法住智), which knows it as the Buddha taught it, and **genuine wisdom** (真實智), which observes it directly. We met the pair on Day 3. Study gives the first; meditation and insight, the second.

Dependent origination was "never made" by anyone, not even the Buddha. "Whether Tathāgatas appear or not", the nature of things stands. The treatise calls this the "realm of things" (法界). Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 here means cause; the nature of things is the cause of their standing.

"Consciousness through feeling, drawn forth by ignorance and formations, is the **sprout** of suffering. Craving through becoming **tends** it. Birth and old age and death are the **tree** of suffering." The projected links are the sprout; the generating links water it; the fruit is a whole life.

Why does the sprout not wither? Venerable Miào Jìng: "because this feeling is associated with ignorance, it protects the contaminated seeds from withering and gradually makes them stronger." Every unexamined feeling waters the sprout.

The same links as a **lamp**: consciousness through feeling is the wick; ignorance, formations, craving, grasping, and becoming are the oil; birth and old age and death are the flame. The flame looks continuous but is renewed every instant from wick and oil. Take away the oil and the lamp goes out by itself. Compare Day 43's lamp, which needed no self to keep burning.

Two counts of knowledge from the Āgamas: seven knowledges for each link (knowing the link, its arising, its cessation, the path, in past, present, and future) make seventy-seven, not eighty-four, because, Venerable Miào Jìng notes, ignorance's seven are omitted. Four knowledges for each of eleven links make forty-four.

Six **direct realisations** (現觀) sever the three defilements. Ru-Yi's note takes the last as an arhat's; Venerable Miào Jìng places it at Buddhahood, after the ten bodhisattva stages, "merit fully perfected". It is a Mahāyāna reading of an early list.

"The Ground with Applied and Sustained Thought, the Ground without Applied but with Sustained Thought, and the Ground without Either have been explained." Stages three to five of the seventeen are done.
Seventy-five days have taken us through the first five of the seventeen stages. Their shape:

items: **Stages 1–2 (fascicles 1–3):** the mind, from a single moment of seeing to the classification of everything knowable.

**Stages 3–5 (fascicles 4–10):** the three realms surveyed; causation; right and wrong attention, with sixteen refuted doctrines; and defilement: affliction, karma, and rebirth as dependent origination.

blocks.text: The direction from here changes. Fascicle 11 begins the sixth stage, **meditative absorption** (三摩呬多地): having understood how the mind binds itself, the treatise turns to how it is trained.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, by how many kinds of wisdom is dependent origination known?
options: two — the wisdom abiding in the teaching, and genuine wisdom
quiz.why: "By two: the wisdom that abides in the teaching, and genuine wisdom." The first knows it as the Buddha revealed it; the second observes its profound meaning as one who has glimpsed the path. Venerable Miào Jìng: the *Āgamas* call genuine wisdom "nirvāṇa-wisdom."

quiz.q: The text says the standing of things takes the nature of things as its cause, "so it is called the realm of things." How do the teachers explain 法界?
options: the relationship between nature and standing
界 means cause — the nature of things causes their standing, so the nature itself is the realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Only with the nature of things as cause is there their standing — so the nature of things is the realm of things. 界 means cause." Venerable Miào Jìng agrees; the note's "relationship between the two" differs. The Buddha said dependent origination "is not something I made, nor is it something anyone else made."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the sprout, the tending, and the tree of suffering?
options: consciousness through feeling is the sprout; craving through becoming tends it; birth and old age-death are the tree
quiz.why: "Consciousness through feeling, drawn forth by ignorance and formations as their condition, is the sprout of suffering. Craving through becoming … tends and waters the sprout. Birth and old-age-and-death … are the tree of suffering." Venerable Miào Jìng: the sprout is the seeds projected by ignorance and formations.

quiz.q: Why does feeling keep the contaminated seed — the sprout — from withering, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: this feeling is bound up with ignorance, so it protects the contaminated seeds from withering and makes them stronger
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Because this feeling is associated with ignorance, it protects the contaminated seeds from withering and gradually makes them strong." Hence craving through becoming, drawn forth by feeling, "tends and waters" the sprout.

quiz.q: Using a lamp, which links are the wick, the oil, and the flame?
options: consciousness through feeling the wick; ignorance, formations, craving, grasping, becoming the oil; birth and old age-death the flame
quiz.why: "Which links … should be understood as a lamp's wick? Consciousness through feeling. Which as its oil? Ignorance, formations, craving, grasping, and becoming. Which as its flame? Birth and old-age-and-death." Venerable Miào Jìng: the wick is the centre of life.

quiz.q: The text says seven knowledges per link make seventy-seven. Twelve times seven is eighty-four — why seventy-seven, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: ignorance's seven are omitted — only eleven links get seven each
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Seventy-seven means seven are missing — the seven for ignorance." Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from ignorance, each of eleven links has seven knowledges; forty-four is eleven links times the four truths.

quiz.q: Six direct realisations sever the three defilements. The reading note says the final one is an arhat's. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: through the first to tenth bodhisattva grounds, only at buddhahood is it final, with merit fully complete
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "One must pass the first ground, second … tenth, and at buddhahood comes 'final realisation,' merit fully perfected"; the realisation of the truths through wisdom is fundamental wisdom, the bordering one subsequent wisdom. The note's "arhat" differs (logged).
